newsitem.title: FRANCE: French finance ministry clarifies on GAN.
newsitem.headline: French finance ministry clarifies on GAN.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn did not state a position on the privatisation of insurance group GAN during a hearing at the National Assembly's finance committee on Wednesday, a finance ministry official said.
The minister limited himself to restating the situation and the facts of the case, said the official.

Earlier, a parliamentary source had reported Strauss-Kahn as saying that the group would need 10 billion francs more than had been forecast and that France's European partners would impose privatisation.

The finance ministry official stressed that Strauss-Kahn had said GAN's financial needs would exceed 10 billion, and not 10 billion more than had been forecast, as the parliamentary source had quoted him as saying.
"It was a restatement on the negotiations with Brussels," said the ministry official.

The previous centre-right government had proposed a rescue package of 20-billion-francs and said 11 million would be given in the form of a capital injection this year once approval had been granted by the European Commission in Brussels, which vets state aid to companies in the European Union.
Strauss-Kahn had reminded the finance committee that the Commission had stipulated when approving a previous aid package in 1996 that GAN's bank subsidiary CIC be privatised.
He noted that the new package had been submitted with a new commitment to privatise parent insurance company itself.

"At the moment, in the talks with Brussels designed to allow the recapitalisation -- the 11 billion earmarked for this year -- the Commission has taken on board these two elements," the official said.
